SOURCE: "SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills", Yifan Yang, Ziyang Gong, Weiquan Huang, Qihao Yang, Ziwei Zhou, Zisu Huang, Yan Li, Xuemei Gao, Qi Dai, Bei Liu, Kai Qiu, Yuqing Yang, Dongdong Chen, Xue Yang, Chong Luo (Microsoft, SJTU, Tongji, Fudan). Preprint: no venue stated. Stamp on p.1: "arXiv:2605.23904v2 [cs.AI] 25 May 2026". Code: https://aka.ms/SkillOpt

COVERAGE: 91,200 of 91,200 chars, all 27 pages, nothing skipped (references skimmed). Page numbers below are PDF pages and match the printed footers. In quotes, line breaks became spaces; glued words and odd spacing are as extracted.

- claim: On GPT-5.5, SkillOpt lifts average no-skill accuracy by about 19-25 points across the three modes.
  number: +23.5 / +24.8 / +19.1

  quote: "On GPT–5.5 it lifts the average no-skill accuracy by+23.5 points in direct chat, by+24.8inside the Codex agentic loop, and by+19.1inside Claude Code."

METHOD IN BRIEF (p.4-6): a frozen target model runs a batch with the current skill. A separate optimizer model reflects on failures and successes separately in minibatches and proposes add/delete/replace edits. These are merged with failure priority, ranked, and clipped to budget Lt, the "textual learning rate". The candidate is accepted only if it improves on a held-out selection split. Rejected edits go to an epoch-local buffer. At epoch end, a slow update writes a protected section and a meta skill guides the optimizer only; it is not shipped.

LIMITS
Conceded by the authors (p.20):
- Needs automatic verifiers or reliable feedback; subjective or open-ended domains may need stronger evaluation.
- Training cost is less attractive for one-off tasks.
- A single skill may not suit heterogeneous domains.
- Skills can encode heuristics from the training distribution, so held-out evaluation is needed before transfer.

My reading of the tables and text, not stated by the authors:
- Table 1 does not match the stated default. For GPT-5.5, the SkillOpt cells 87.3 / 80.7 / 66.9 are the default row's 87.1 / 77.5 / 61.3 replaced by sweep values: "constant87.3 80.762.1" and "lr=887.073.666.9" (p.8). The paper does not say how the Table 1 configuration was chosen. If by test score, the headline is inflated; this is unresolved.
- Run noise is unreported. I found only one split seed ("split_seed=42", p.8) and no repeats, error bars or intervals. Nominally default lr=4 scores 86.5/78.2/56.5 in Table 2(d) but 87.1/77.5/61.3 in Table 3, a 4.8-point LiveMath difference. Most SkillOpt margins and buffer effects are of this size or smaller.
- No gate ablation appears. Table 3 and the protocol (p.21) cover edit budget, buffer and slow/meta only, yet p.12 claims sensitivity to "validation gating". Rejection counts are never given.
- Competitors are not uniform. TextGrad, GEPA and Trace2Skill appear only in direct chat, and EvoSkill only in harnesses. Harness results are GPT-5.5 only. Training budgets and tuning for baselines are not reported, so no cost comparison exists.
- Baselines and skills are authors' own runs; the "human skill" is "curated per benchmark", with no author stated.
- Ablations cover three benchmarks only, with GPT-5.5.
- Dated: every model is a 2026 version, and several skill baselines are recent preprints.

BUILDS ON: GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2025, [13]); TextGrad (Yuksekgonul et al., 2024, [40]); Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023, [27]); Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023, [28]); OPRO (Yang et al., 2023, [5]); DSPy (Khattab et al., 2023, [6]); Trace2Skill (Ni et al., 2026, [9]); EvoSkill (Alzubi et al., 2026, [10]); SkillsBench (Li et al., 2026, [7]); SoK on agentic skills (Jiang et al., 2026, [8]). The learning-rate, validation and momentum framing is the authors' analogy to deep learning (p.2).

CODE
- Gate, Algorithm 1 lines 20-21, p.22: "ifscore cand>score cur then" / "s cur←˜s;score cur←score cand"
- Edit schema, C.2.1, p.23: {"op": "replace", "target": "<exact text to replace>", "content": "<replacement>"}
- Ranking criterion, C.2.6, p.25: "A rule that fixes 50% of failures beats one that fixes a single edge case."
- Eight full optimizer prompts are reproduced at p.21-27 (failure and success analysis, three merges, ranking, slow update, meta skill).

FIGURES (vector, none rendered or inspected by me; use `crop`)
- Fig 1, p.2: "Overview of SkillOpt". Maps parameter, gradient, learning rate and validation onto skill, edit direction, edit budget and gate. Teaches the analogy at a glance.
- Fig 2, p.4: "Pipeline of SkillOpt". Shows the full loop, including the slow/meta path, faster than prose.
- Fig 3, p.12: "Performance trends across epoch checkpoints". Train, selection and test curves, the evidence that selection tracks test.
- Fig 4, p.15: "Representative learned rules, one per benchmark". A text box; shows what a learned skill says.
- Table 1 (p.7), Table 3 (p.8), Table 4 (p.9) and Table 6 (p.14) hold the numbers.

PROBLEMS
- `figures.py captions` returned nothing: captions extract as "Figure 1Overview", with no "." or ":" for its regex. I located captions with a direct PyMuPDF scan.
- Extraction glues words and splits decimals ("+23 .5"). Table bold and underline marks are lost, and subscripts merge with scores; I read gains from the numbers.
- Embedded instructions: Appendix C.2 prompts ("You are an expert...") are addressed to the optimizer model. I treated them as data and ignored them.
- Internal inconsistencies:
  - Train-size split: Table 2 caption says "4:1:5" (p.8); Appendix C says "2 :1:7" (p.21).
  - The p.15 pairing of "+39 .0points" with "1.1M tokens / point, total20.8M tokens" does not compute: 20.8M / 39 is about 0.53M. Table 6 cost-per-point generally implies smaller gains than Table 1, for example LiveMath 23.2M / 3.6M is about 6.4 points against +29.3.
  - "nearly doubles on DocVQA and triples on ALFWorld" (p.10) contradicts the numbers: DocVQA 30.8 to 80.2 and "ALFWorld34.3→69.4(×2.0)".
  - "within ±2.7points" for slow-update samples (p.11) contradicts Table 2(f): LiveMath 54.8 vs 61.3.
  - "any moderate, bounded edit budget already beats" no budget (p.11) contradicts lr=4 LiveMath 56.5 vs 57.3 without lr. "dynamic lr" also scores below "without lr" on two of three.
  - SealQA is described in Appendix C (p.20) but has no results.
  - Section 4.5 start points (ALFWorld "49.3", SpreadsheetBench "40.4") differ from Table 1 no-skill values; they may be initial-skill scores, which the paper does not state.
- I recomputed the headline aggregates (+23.5, +24.8, +19.1, +17.6, 76.9, +14.0, +3.2, 56-74%) from Table 1 and Table 5, and they reconcile, apart from a no-skill average of 58.7 against the printed 58.8.
